name: Ruby 18

origin.regionNote: Yuchi / Sun Moon Lake is the classic garden; the cultivar travels

categoryNote: English black tea is 红茶, named for the liquor. Chinese 黑茶 is the post-fermented class this atlas files as dark.

harvest.note: Summer leaf is often the loud mint-cinnamon lot. This is not the high-mountain oolong calendar.

pluckStandard: one bud and two leaves, orthodox strip

processing.description: TTES No. 18 — 紅玉. The tea experiment station’s published parentage is Burma large-leaf B-729 × Taiwan wild B-607, named in 1999. English write-ups disagree on how long the trials ran; this atlas keeps the station’s parentage and the naming year, and does not freeze a folklore chronology.
Orthodox black-tea make on a large-leaf hybrid.
Full oxidation. The mint-cinnamon (wintergreen) note is the cultivar, not a flavouring.

profile.mouthfeel: round, medium-full, less punchy than Assam

water.note: Near boiling, medium mineral. The mint reads more clearly if you do not stew it.

storage: Airtight, opaque. Orthodox blacks last 18–24 months well.

qualityMarkers.test: whole twisted leaf you can unfurl; grains from a cutter are a different tea
if it tastes of added flavouring oil, it is not this cultivar doing the work

qualityMarkers.claim: TTES No. 18 / 紅玉 named on the bag

commonFaults.name: generic Taiwanese black sold as Ruby

compare.differentiator: Both large-leaf orthodox blacks. Ruby’s mint-cinnamon is a Taiwanese hybrid; Dian Hong is Yunnan daye malt and sweet potato.

summary: Taiwan’s named black: TTES No. 18 from Yuchi, orthodox, with a mint-cinnamon register no mainland black shares.
